newsitem.title: THAILAND: Ex-Khmer Rouge said to dodge assassination attempt.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Khmer Rouge said to dodge assassination attempt.

text.p: Khmer Rouge defectors tried to kill a former top leader of the guerrilla group in a disagreement on whether to support the government of powerful Cambodian leader Hun Sen, the former rebel's personal secretary said on Monday.
Ei Chien, an ex-Khmer Rouge commander who is now mayor of the northwest Cambodian town of Pailin, was attacked by 10 fellow defectors last week, his secretary told Reuters.

"They were about to hit the trigger when Ei Chien jumped to the ground and escaped," the secretary said in a telephone interview from the gem and timber-rich town of Pailin, adding that the assailants later escaped to the nearby city of Battambang.
"They said if we would lean closer to the Phnom Penh government, then they could be promoted to a higher rank in the army," he said.

The attackers apparently wanted to ally Pailin -- where the secretary said the situation remained tense -- with Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on July 6.

Ei Chien has remained neutral since the coup, although hardline Khmer Rouge have said he agreed to help them fight with Ranariddh's rag-tag army, now holding out against Hun Sen's forces in a shrinking pocket in Cambodia's northwest.
The Khmer Rouge, architects of the 1975-79 "killing fields" regime, have long been a divisive element in Cambodian politics.

They signed a 1991 peace pact that paved the way for U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993 but later reneged on the deal and fought the coalition government which Ranariddh and Hun Sen formed following the polls.
But a year ago the Khmer Rouge began unravelling when a wave of defections led by former Khmer Rouge Foreign Minister Ieng Sary severely weakened their ranks.

Ei Chien, who was Ieng Sary's commander for Pailin, was allowed to turn his former military base into an autonomous zone. Ei Chien became mayor and is vice president of a political movement made up of former Khmer Rouge.
The decline of the Khmer Rouge increased worsening tensions between Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who vied to recruit rebels to their own sides.
Ranariddh was on the verge of completing a peace deal with the last of the rebels in the northwest stronghold of Anlong Veng when Hun Sen overthrew him.
More than one million Cambodians died during the Khmer Rouge regime from execution, starvation, disease and overwork.
